claims.text: The proposed framework achieved an F1-score of 0.968-0.983 when trained on the full dataset of 700 patient notes.
The proposed framework achieved an F1-score of 0.960-0.973 when trained on a few-shot subset of 100 patient notes.
The two-phase framework reduced hallucinated features by 89.9% on the private dataset compared to the baseline LLM with few-shot in-context learning.
The two-phase framework reduced missing features by 88.9% on the private dataset compared to the baseline LLM with few-shot in-context learning.
Expected calibration error increased from 0.060 to 0.147 during calibration evaluation on few-shot training.
Brier score improved from 0.087 to 0.036 during calibration evaluation on few-shot training.
The average model confidence remained stable at 0.84 (SD 0.003) despite F1 improvements from 0.819 to 0.986.

evidence.description: The framework achieved an F1-score of 0.968-0.983 on the full dataset of 700 patient notes.
Achieved 0.960-0.973 with a few-shot subset of 100 of 700 patient notes.
It reduced hallucinations by 89.9% (from 3081 to 311 features) on the private dataset compared with the baseline LLM.
It reduced missing features by 88.9% (from 6376 to 708) on the private dataset compared with the baseline LLM.
Calibration evaluation on few-shot training showed that the expected calibration error increased from 0.060 to 0.147.
The Brier score improved from 0.087 to 0.036.
The average model confidence remained stable at 0.84 (SD 0.003) despite F1 improvements from 0.819 to 0.986.

methodologies.name: Two-Phase LLM Fine-Tuning Framework
methodologies.description: A two-phase framework combining instruction fine-tuning to teach feature extraction with confidence-regularization fine-tuning to penalize overconfident incorrect predictions.
datasets: United States Medical Licensing Examination Step-2 Clinical Skills dataset

limitations.text: Traditional calibration metrics show misalignment as expected calibration error increased from 0.060 to 0.147 on few-shot training.
